subject: Hosted API vs Dedicated — latency/throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>, Morgan Reyes <morgan.reyes@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up: latency & throughput needs for inference

Hi Alex & Morgan,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about FinPay's fraud-scoring pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of requirements you mentioned:
- Peak traffic: ~500–750 inference requests per second during payment windows; sustained baseline ~150–200 rps.
- Target p99 latency: <= 120 ms for ~512-token responses (most calls are short but we have occasional longer contexts).
- Burst tolerance: short spikes to ~1.5k rps for ~5–10 minutes during promotions.
- Data controls: all PII needs to be isolated; at this stage Hosted is acceptable if we can guarantee no long-term retention and offer network restrictions.

Questions / next steps:
1) Would you prefer we run a short Hosted API load test with request profile you send (we can simulate p99)?
2) If we can’t hit p99 120 ms on Hosted at your burst profile, we recommend moving to a Dedicated capacity tier (reserved GPU pool) — we can scope the expected throughput and cost.
3) Can you share the QPS profile (avg/peak by minute) and a couple of representative payloads?

I attached a quick CSV you can drop your profile into (finpay-qps-profile.csv). If you’re OK, I’ll loop in Marissa to propose a lightweight benchmark plan and timing (aiming for a 48–72 hour pilot).

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: finpay-qps-profile.csv (CSV stub: columns timestamp, rps, token_length)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Morgan Reyes <morgan.reyes@finpay.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: latency & throughput needs for inference

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming peak concurrency: the 500–750 rps is accurate for most days; we have two promotional windows per month that can push sustained ~1.2–1.5k rps for ~8–12 minutes.
- Payloads: typical request is ~200–350 tokens, but ~10% of calls are >512 tokens (these are the ones that bump latency).
- Security: Hosted is fine for a pilot provided we can have VPC egress controls and guaranteed no model-training or retention on Redwood's side.

We attached our minute-level profile (finpay-qps-profile.csv). Please run the Hosted API test first — if Hosted can't meet p99 120 ms under the burst profile, we'd be open to a Dedicated conversation.

Also, what's the expected timeline to get results if you start the pilot tomorrow?

Best,
Alex Johnson
Director, Fraud Analytics | FinPay
alex.johnson@finpay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: latency & throughput needs for inference

Hi Alex — looping in as solutions lead. Thanks for the profile, Alex. Proposed plan: 

1) Hosted API pilot (48 hours)
   - We will run two phases: baseline (sustained 200 rps) and burst (simulate your promotion spikes up to 1.5k rps).
   - Metrics: token-level p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, tail CPU/GPU utilization, and TX bytes.
   - Config: prefer to start on Hosted with a "burst-capacity" routing policy + prefix caching enabled; this often covers short spikes without needing Dedicated.

2) If Hosted p99 > 120 ms during burst, we will model Dedicated capacity sizing and provide an expected cost delta (monthly reserved vs Hosted nominal).

3) Security controls: we can enable request-scoped redaction, no-model-training contract clause, and (for pilot) IP allowlist/VPC egress controls. For Private/VPC onboarding we can discuss next phase.

Timeline & logistics:
- We can start the benchmark as early as tomorrow afternoon. We’ll need: your test endpoints (or we can generate synthetic payloads from the CSV), and an email address to send a signed PoC scope (mutual-action-plan.xlsx).
- Estimated results delivered within 72 hours after test completion, with a summary deck and raw logs.

I attached the benchmark plan and a MAP stub: redwood-benchmark-plan.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx.

Let me know what time tomorrow works and I’ll book a 30-min kickoff with engineering.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>

Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: latency & throughput needs for inference

Marissa / Aditya — thanks for the clear plan. We’re happy to start with the Hosted API pilot and validate whether the burst-capacity + caching approach can meet p99 <= 120 ms. If results show Hosted can't meet p99 under realistic burst, we’ll fast-track Dedicated sizing.

Next actions from FinPay:
- I signed the MAP stub and uploaded it to the Drive link you shared.
- I can provide test endpoints and allowlist IPs by tomorrow 9am PDT.
- We need a ballpark quote for Dedicated capacity sizing in case we need to move fast — can you provide an initial estimate range during the pilot?

Decision timeline: pilot this week, decision within 2 weeks after results.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director, Fraud Analytics | FinPay
alex.johnson@finpay.com
